intro: The HTML and platform fundamentals behind accessible, fast pages.

entries.short: Use elements for what they mean, not how they look.
entries.medium: button, nav, article, main and friends carry meaning that screen readers, search engines and reader modes use. Native elements also bring keyboard behaviour and focus for free.
entries.detail: The first rule of ARIA is to prefer a native element over adding a role to a div. Most accessibility bugs are really semantics bugs.

entries.short: Both download in parallel; defer runs after parsing and keeps order.
entries.medium: defer executes after the HTML is parsed, in source order, just before DOMContentLoaded. async runs as soon as it downloads, in any order, and can interrupt parsing. type=module is deferred by default.
entries.detail: Use defer or modules for app code that depends on order and the DOM. Use async only for independent scripts like analytics.

entries.short: Incremental and error-tolerant; the DOM can differ from the source.
entries.medium: The parser repairs bad markup, inserting tbody and closing tags, so the DOM is not always the source you wrote. Scripts without defer or async block the parser; CSS blocks rendering but not parsing.
entries.detail: This timing is exactly why defer, async and DOMContentLoaded exist.

entries.short: Valid custom attributes for extra data on an element.
entries.medium: Read through dataset in camelCase; values are always strings. Good for passing server-rendered values to scripts and for behaviour hooks.
entries.detail: Do not use them for state that assistive tech needs. Use ARIA or native attributes there.

entries.short: label for=id or wrap the input, so the field is named.
entries.medium: The association makes the field announce its name and lets a click focus or toggle it. Groups of radios or checkboxes are named with fieldset and legend. Placeholders are not labels.
entries.detail: Every control needs an accessible name. Icon-only buttons need aria-label or visually hidden text.

entries.short: A div is not focusable, has no role and ignores the keyboard.
entries.medium: A button is focusable, activates on Enter and Space, is announced as a button and submits forms. Faking it with a div needs role, tabindex and key handlers, and still misses form behaviour.
entries.detail: Use an anchor for navigation and a button for actions. Getting the div right costs more than using the element that already works.

entries.short: header, nav, main, aside and footer let users jump around.
entries.medium: Landmarks give a screen reader user a map of the page. Headings give an outline. main should appear once per page, and heading levels should not skip for visual reasons.
entries.detail: These structures are also what reader modes and search engines use to find the main content.

entries.short: alt describes the image, or is empty if it is decorative.
entries.medium: Meaningful images need alt text that conveys the same information. Decorative images use alt="" so they are skipped. Add width and height to reserve space and avoid layout shift.
entries.detail: Lazy-load offscreen images with loading="lazy" and decoding="async", but keep the hero eager for LCP.

entries.short: Input types and constraints give validation and better keyboards for free.
entries.medium: type=email, tel, url, number and date bring mobile keyboards and basic validation. required, min, max, maxlength and pattern add constraints. autocomplete helps autofill.
entries.detail: Native validation is a first line, not a replacement for server-side validation, which is the one that matters for security.

entries.short: Tells mobile browsers to use the device width.
entries.medium: width=device-width, initial-scale=1 makes the layout match the device and prevents the browser from zooming out. Without it, media queries behave as if the page were desktop width.
entries.detail: Do not disable zoom by setting maximum-scale or user-scalable=no, which blocks users who need to magnify.

entries.short: title, description and Open Graph shape search and sharing.
entries.medium: Each page needs a unique, descriptive title and a meta description. Open Graph tags control the preview when the link is shared. A canonical link avoids duplicate-content issues.
entries.detail: The title is what a screen reader announces first and what search results show, so write it for humans, not keywords.

entries.short: It changes what is announced, not what the element does.
entries.medium: ARIA names, roles and states describe custom widgets to assistive tech, but it adds no behaviour. role=button still needs keyboard handling. aria-label names an element; aria-expanded reports state.
entries.detail: The rule: use a native element if one exists, and only reach for ARIA to fill the gap. No ARIA is better than bad ARIA.
